text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: production - gpu-pool-us-west1 scaling stalled. queue length rising for inference-prod (tokenized jobs). Alerting SRE oncall.

morgan: on it, grabbing autoscaler logs. can someone confirm if this is quota or instance provisioning failures?

jia: seeing repeated errors in autoscaler: `QuotaExceeded: Quota 'NVIDIA_TESLA_T4' exceeded for project redwood-prod-legacy in region us-west1.` autoscaler is trying to create instances under `redwood-prod-legacy` account, but our serving env should use `redwood-prod`.

ryan: that smells like the recent terraform drift where the fallback pool still points to legacy project. good catch. how widespread is impact?

elena: CS: customers on standard tier reporting increased latency and occasional 503s starting ~11:10 PDT. tracking severity: degraded for ~12% of requests to the hosted API for the last 20m. not yet customer-facing incident page.

morgan: logs show autoscaler 3x create attempts -> immediate denial from GCP. snippet: ```json
{
  "error": "quotaExceeded",
  "details": "Request for resource 'NVIDIA_TESLA_T4' (or api name) exceeds quota for project redwood-prod-legacy in region us-west1"
}
```

jia: confirmed: autoscaler config `instance_profile.project` was recently templated during a rollout. deployment pipeline set it to `${var.legacy_project}` for the warm pool marker and `autoscaler` inherits it. so scheduler points to wrong project for scale-up.

ryan: mitigation options: 1) patch autoscaler to target correct project (fast) 2) manually request quota increase in legacy project (slow) 3) reroute new traffic to eu-west1 / fallback pool (medium) 4) spin up quantized CPU fallback model (low perf)

morgan: applying option 1 now — update config in k8s/infra and restart autoscaler. doing a canary patch to one region first.

cloud-gcp-bot: GCP API: quota denial logged. Ticket created: 9876543210 for project redwood-prod-legacy - requesting quota review.

jia: FYI patch applied to autoscaler deployment in staging, rolling to prod warm-pool controller. will restart controller, expecting new requests to create instances under `redwood-prod`.

elena: CS update: routing customers on enterprise plans to retry. no public status yet, but prepping message if impact persists >30m.

morgan: patch rolled to one replica in us-west1 warm-pool controller. monitoring create events.

morgan: good: new create attempts now reference `redwood-prod` project. however AWS/GCP capacity in us-west1 is also near saturated for T4s so some creates are pending - still slower than normal.

ryan: start fallback plan B in parallel: change routing policy to send 25% of traffic to eu-west1 pool and lower model size for non-enterprise customers. can someone update the routing config?

jia: making routing change (live). command: ```bash
# temporary route 25% of requests to eu-west1
redwood route set --from inference-prod --to inference-eu-west1 --percentage 25
```
jia: applied. verifying logs.

elena: CS: after routing change we see error rate down to ~6% and latency on impacted requests increased ~120ms avg. enterprise customers unaffected.

morgan: also enabling CPU-quantized fallback for lowest-priority tenants to reduce queue pressure. `model_variant=quant-v2-cpu` for premium:false. doing rollout now.

cloud-gcp-bot: New instance create succeeded: 3 x n1-standard-8 + T4 attached in project redwood-prod in us-west1.

morgan: autoscaler stable after config fix and small capacity came up. queue length trending down. monitoring for 15m before closing.

elena: customer impact summary so far: peak affected window ~11:10-11:55 PDT. ~12% degraded error/timeout rate at peak, reduced to ~2-4% after routing + fallback. CS drafted a proactive note for customers affected more than 10 requests; holding for final numbers.

ryan: root cause (initial): rollout templating caused autoscaler to target wrong GCP project which had stricter quotas and no warm pool. contributing: overall regional T4 scarcity amplifying impact.

morgan: action items: 1) roll back the templating change and add tests to catch project drift (owner: infra-team) 2) add autoscaler validation to fail fast if create requests reference non-prod project (owner: eng-sre) 3) run capacity burn tests in us-west1 weekly to detect saturation (owner: infra) 4) CS follow-up + customer comm (owner: elena).

elena: filing follow-up checklist and customer outreach. will include mitigation timeline and what we did.

jia: posting link to PR that fixed template: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4523 - change is small.

morgan: closing loop: queue normalized at 11:52 PDT, autoscaler healthy, will keep monitoring. tagging for postmortem. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident marked as resolved by morgan. Duration: 42m. Postmortem requested.
